panels.description: Modest Keel apartment at dusk with quilts, repaired furniture, old books, family photographs, recycled-container plants and ration-marked water jugs. Grandmother folds a cloth; the tall bookshelf and its book-width gap dominate the wall. Alex stands in the doorway. Leave upper-left clear.
Alex stands in the doorway with eyes briefly closed, gently correcting Grandmother. Leave upper-left clear.
Alex kneels beside Grandmother’s chair while she folds the cloth. Leave upper corners clear.
Grandmother’s face becomes suddenly precise and clear. Leave upper-left open.
Grandmother’s frail hand points toward the worn hand-bound book with a faint balanced water-drop symbol. Keep hand and book unobstructed.
Alex reaches toward the book from behind the shelf, framed by warm apartment light. Grandmother remains seated below. Keep book and face clear.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Of course. Alex. I knew that. Did your father come home yet?

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Adrian, get down the book you put up there. The one you want Alex to have when he turns eighteen.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Careful. He said it was worth protecting.
